A prisoner arranged with a prison guard to escape by hiding inside a coffin during a funeral procession. Once the coffin had been taken beyond the prison walls and buried, the guard was supposed to dig him out and help him escape. The prisoner entered the coffin expecting the guard to be alive and waiting outside to rescue him; he did not know the guard had died and had been placed in the coffin for his own funeral. After the burial, the prisoner struck a match, saw the guard’s body, and realized the escape plan had failed. With the coffin buried and no one left to free him or summon help, he died trapped inside. The match revealed the fatal failure; it did not cause the danger.

When he struck a match and recognized the dead guard, he understood that the person meant to rescue him was instead buried beside him. Trapped underground with no one to release him or summon help, he died. The match exposed the failed plan; it did not itself cause his death.

When he struck a match and recognized the guard, he realized the promised rescue could not happen. Trapped underground with no way to open the coffin or summon help, he died.
